facts.fact: According to Wyzowl's 2021 State of Video Marketing report, 87% of video marketers report that video gives them a positive return on investment (ROI).

facts.fact: Traditionally, cost per completed view (CPCV) prices between $0.10-0.30 for video ads.
facts.quote: Traditionally, CPCV prices between $0.10-0.30, but alternative formats such as native outstream perform at an average of $0.02.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that native outstream video ad formats perform at an average CPCV of $0.02.
facts.quote: alternative formats such as native outstream perform at an average of $0.02.

facts.fact: Cost per completed view (CPCV) is calculated by dividing total ad spend by the number of completed video views.
facts.quote: CPCV is calculated by dividing your total ad spend by the number of completed video views.

facts.fact: Cost per completed view (CPCV) measures the amount paid by an advertiser to the publisher once a video has been viewed through to completion.
facts.quote: Cost per completed view (CPCV) measures the amount paid by an advertiser to the publisher once a video has been viewed through to completion.

facts.fact: Watch time measures the exact amount of seconds a viewer watched a video, while completion rate measures how many viewers watched the video in full.
facts.quote: Watch time measures the exact amount of seconds that a viewer watched, and completion rate measures how many viewers watched your video in full.

facts.fact: Completion rate is the percentage of times a video played to the end, whereas completes are reported as a count of times 100% of the video was viewed.
facts.quote: Completion rate is the percentage of times the video played to the end, whereas completes are presented as a number.

facts.fact: Quartile completion tracks the number of impressions for which an ad clip played to the end of the first quarter of the video's total length.
facts.quote: It tracks the number of impressions for which an ad clip played to the end of the first quarter of the video’s total length.
